Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106754; File No. SR-CboeBZX-2026-086]
October 28, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 15, 2026, Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “BZX”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe BZX Exchange, Inc. (“BZX” or the “Exchange”) is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission” or “SEC”) a proposed rule change to amend Rule 11.1(a) to adopt a Start Time order instruction, based on the Start Time instruction adopted by its affiliated exchange, Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc. (“EDGX”). The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​bzx/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.1(a) to adopt a “Start Time” order instruction that would permit a User to designate, in thirty-minute increments prior to the commencement
(
printed page 69019)
of Regular Trading Hours,
[
5
]
the time at which an order entered prior to Regular Trading Hours becomes eligible for execution. The proposed rule change is based on EDGX Rule 11.1(a)(2),
[
6
]
but the Exchange is proposing to adopt only the Start Time instruction and related provisions. The Exchange intends to implement the proposed rule change on December 7, 2026, in coordination with the implementation of the Start Time instruction on EDGX, so that Members have access to consistent order handling functionality across the Cboe-affiliated equities exchanges.
Current Rule
Under current Rule 11.1(a), Users may enter orders into the System from 2:30 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time (“ET”).
[
7
]
Orders entered between 2:30 a.m. and 4:00 a.m. are not eligible for execution until the start of the Early Trading Session,
[
8
]
Pre-Opening Session,
[
9
]
or Regular Trading Hours, depending on the Time in Force
[
10
]
selected by the User. The current rule provides for two fixed start times within the Early Trading Session. At the commencement of the Early Trading Session, orders entered between 2:30 a.m. and 4:00 a.m. become eligible for execution (a “4:00 a.m. Start”), unless designated as eligible for execution during the Early Trading Session beginning at 7:00 a.m. (a “7:00 a.m. Start”). Orders with a 7:00 a.m. Start designation may be entered between 2:30 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. At each start time, orders are handled in time sequence, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and are placed on the BZX Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with the terms of the order.
Current Rule 11.1(a) also provides that the Exchange will not accept the following orders prior to 7:00 a.m.: BZX Post Only Orders,
[
11
]
ISOs,
[
12
]
BZX Market Orders
[
13
]
that are not Stop Orders
[
14
]
or Eligible Auction Orders as defined in Rule 11.23(a)(8), Minimum Quantity Orders
[
15
]
that also include a Time in Force of Regular Hours Only, and all orders with a Time in Force of IOC
[
16
]
or FOK.
[
17
]
The rule also contains a sentence providing that, at the commencement of the Early Trading Session, orders entered between 6:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. will be handled in time sequence and placed on the BZX Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with their terms. That sentence is inconsistent with the current 2:30 a.m. order entry window and is superseded by the 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start provisions described above.
Proposed Start Time Instruction
The Exchange proposes to delete the 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start designations, together with the superseded sentence relating to orders entered between 6:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m., and to replace them with a flexible Start Time instruction. As proposed, in addition to the Time in Force, a User may also designate a start time for an order (“Start Time”). Start Times may be designated in thirty-minute increments and must be set to a time prior to the commencement of Regular Trading Hours; Start Times may not be designated during Regular Trading Hours. This language is substantively identical to the Start Time language in EDGX Rule 11.1(a)(2), which replaced EDGX's 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start designations with the same flexible and uniform framework. Because orders on the Exchange are not eligible for execution prior to the commencement of the Early Trading Session at 4:00 a.m., the earliest Start Time that will have practical effect is 4:00 a.m., and the latest permissible Start Time is 9:00 a.m.
The Exchange also proposes to provide that, at the commencement of the Early Trading Session and at each Start Time, orders will be handled in time sequence, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and will be placed on the BZX Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with the terms of the order. This provision is consistent with the sequencing provision adopted by EDGX, which provides that, at each Start Time, orders will be handled in time sequence beginning with the oldest time stamp.
[
18
]
The Exchange proposes to retain the reference to the commencement of the Early Trading Session so that orders that are entered prior to the Early Trading Session without a Start Time designation continue to become eligible for execution, in time sequence, at the commencement of the Early Trading Session, as they do today.
For example, a User may enter an order at 5:15 a.m. with a Start Time of 8:00 a.m. That order would be accepted but would not be eligible for execution until 8:00 a.m., at which time it would be handled in time sequence with all other orders designated with an 8:00 a.m. Start Time, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and would be placed on the BZX Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with its terms.
Order Acceptance Restrictions
The Exchange proposes to amend the order acceptance restrictions in Rule 11.1(a) so that they apply prior to 7:00 a.m. or, if later, prior to the order's designated Start Time. The Exchange is not proposing any change to the categories of orders subject to these restrictions, which will continue to be: BZX Post Only Orders, ISOs, BZX Market Orders that are not Stop Orders or Eligible Auction Orders as defined in Rule 11.23(a)(8), Minimum Quantity Orders that also include a Time in Force of Regular Hours Only, and all orders with a Time in Force of IOC or FOK. The Exchange is also retaining the existing 7:00 a.m. threshold. Under the proposal, an order in one of these categories designated with a Start Time later than 7:00 a.m. will not be accepted prior to its Start Time. The current restrictions are designed to limit certain order types that are not suitable for queueing to the period in which an order is eligible for execution and, in the case of the 7:00 a.m. Start, already apply until the time at which an order with a 7:00 a.m. Start designation becomes eligible for execution. Tying the restrictions to an order's designated Start Time applies that same rationale to the more flexible Start Time framework. EDGX similarly ties the same five categories of restrictions to the period before orders become eligible for execution, which on EDGX is the Order Acceptance Queueing Time.
[
19
]
The Exchange is not proposing to change its order entry window, which will continue to begin at 2:30 a.m., or the Time in Force instructions available to Users. Orders entered prior to the Early Trading Session without a Start Time designation will continue to become eligible for execution at the start of the Early Trading Session, Pre-
(
printed page 69020)
Opening Session, or Regular Trading Hours, depending on the Time in Force selected by the User. Use of the Start Time instruction is optional.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
20
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
21
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes the proposed Start Time instruction removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system because it replaces the fixed 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start designations with a flexible and uniform framework. Under that framework, Members may control the time at which their orders become eligible for execution prior to Regular Trading Hours. The Commission approved the same Start Time framework for EDGX, which replaced EDGX's 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start construct.
[
22
]
The Start Time instruction provides Members with additional flexibility to manage the timing of their order flow in the period before Regular Trading Hours. This includes aligning order eligibility with anticipated market conditions or with their own trading strategies, without requiring Members to manually enter orders at a particular time.
The Exchange believes the proposed time-sequencing provision promotes just and equitable principles of trade and protects investors because orders that become eligible at the commencement of the Early Trading Session or at a given Start Time will be handled in a transparent and objective manner, in time sequence beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp. This is the same manner in which orders are handled today at the commencement of the Early Trading Session and at each of the 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start, and it is consistent with the sequencing provision approved for EDGX.
The Exchange believes that tying the existing order acceptance restrictions to the later of 7:00 a.m. or the order's designated Start Time protects investors and the public interest. The proposal preserves the existing categories of restricted orders and the existing 7:00 a.m. threshold. It applies those restrictions consistently to orders that will not be eligible for execution until a later Start Time, ensuring that order types that are not suitable for queueing are not accepted before the order may execute. The proposed rule change does not loosen any existing restriction.
The proposed rule change also promotes consistency across the Cboe-affiliated equities exchanges, which reduces complexity for Members that access multiple Cboe-affiliated exchanges and fosters cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities. The proposed rule change does not permit unfair discrimination because the Start Time instruction will be available to all Members on the same terms, and its use is optional.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition because the Start Time instruction will be available to all Members on an equal and non-discriminatory basis, and its use is optional. The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition because it is based on a rule that the Commission approved for EDGX, and it is designed to provide Members with consistent order handling functionality across the Cboe-affiliated equities exchanges rather than to address any competitive issue. Other exchanges are free to adopt similar functionality.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not:
A. significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest;
B. impose any significant burden on competition; and

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106753; File No. SR-CboeEDGA-2026-035]
October 28, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (the “Act”),
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 15, 2026, Cboe EDGA Exchange, Inc. (the “Exchange” or “EDGA”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II, and III below, which Items have been prepared by the Exchange. The Exchange filed the proposal as a “non-controversial” proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
Cboe EDGA Exchange, Inc. (“EDGA” or the “Exchange”) is filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission” or “SEC”) a proposed rule change to amend Rule 11.1(a)(1) to adopt a Start Time order instruction, based on the Start Time instruction adopted by its affiliated exchange, Cboe EDGX Exchange, Inc. (“EDGX”). The text of the proposed rule change is provided in Exhibit 5.
The text of the proposed rule change is also available on the Commission's website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
), the Exchange's website (
https://www.cboe.com/​us/​equities/​regulation/​rule_​filings/​edga/​
), and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the Exchange included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 11.1(a)(1) to adopt a “Start Time” order instruction that would permit a User to designate, in thirty-minute increments prior to the commencement of Regular Trading Hours,
[
5
]
the time at which an order entered prior to Regular Trading Hours becomes eligible for execution. The proposed rule change is based on EDGX Rule 11.1(a)(2),
[
6
]
but the Exchange is proposing to adopt only the Start Time instruction and related provisions. The Exchange intends to implement the proposed rule change on December 7, 2026, in coordination with the implementation of the Start Time instruction on EDGX, so that Members have access to consistent order handling functionality across the Cboe-affiliated equities exchanges.
Current Rule
Under current Rule 11.1(a)(1), Users may enter orders into the System from 6:00 a.m. until 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time (“ET”).
[
7
]
Orders entered between 6:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. are not eligible for execution until the start of the Early Trading Session,
[
8
]
Pre-Opening Session,
[
9
]
or Regular Trading Hours, depending on the Time in Force
[
10
]
selected by the User. At the commencement of the Early Trading Session, orders entered between 6:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m. are handled in time sequence, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and are placed on the EDGA Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with the terms of the order. The current rule therefore provides a single, fixed point (the commencement of the Early Trading Session at 7:00 a.m.) at which orders entered prior to the Early Trading Session become eligible for execution, and does not permit a User to designate a later point prior to Regular Trading Hours at which an order becomes eligible.
Current Rule 11.1(a)(1) also provides that the Exchange will not accept the following orders prior to 7:00 a.m.: orders with a Post Only instruction,
[
11
]
ISOs,
[
12
]
Market Orders
[
13
]
other than those with a TIF instruction of Regular Hours Only or a Stop Price,
[
14
]
orders with a Minimum Execution Quantity
[
15
]
instruction that also include a TIF instruction of Regular Hours Only, and
(
printed page 69025)
all orders with a TIF instruction of IOC
[
16
]
or FOK.
[
17
]
Proposed Start Time Instruction
The Exchange proposes to amend the time-sequencing provision so that it is no longer limited to orders entered between 6:00 a.m. and 7:00 a.m., and to adopt a flexible Start Time instruction. As proposed, in addition to the Time in Force, a User may also designate a start time for an order (“Start Time”). Start Times may be designated in thirty-minute increments and must be set to a time prior to the commencement of Regular Trading Hours; Start Times may not be designated during Regular Trading Hours. This language is substantively identical to the Start Time language in EDGX Rule 11.1(a)(2), which replaced EDGX's 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start designations with the same flexible and uniform framework. Because orders on the Exchange are not eligible for execution prior to the commencement of the Early Trading Session at 7:00 a.m., the earliest Start Time that will have practical effect is 7:00 a.m., and the latest permissible Start Time is 9:00 a.m.
The Exchange also proposes to provide that, at the commencement of the Early Trading Session and at each Start Time, orders will be handled in time sequence, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and will be placed on the EDGA Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with the terms of the order. This provision is consistent with the sequencing provision adopted by EDGX, which provides that, at each Start Time, orders will be handled in time sequence beginning with the oldest time stamp.
[
18
]
The Exchange proposes to retain the reference to the commencement of the Early Trading Session so that orders that are entered prior to the Early Trading Session without a Start Time designation continue to become eligible for execution, in time sequence, at the commencement of the Early Trading Session, as they do today.
For example, a User may enter an order at 6:15 a.m. with a Start Time of 8:00 a.m. That order would be accepted but would not be eligible for execution until 8:00 a.m., at which time it would be handled in time sequence with all other orders designated with an 8:00 a.m. Start Time, beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp, and would be placed on the EDGA Book, routed, cancelled, or executed in accordance with its terms.
Order Acceptance Restrictions
The Exchange proposes to amend the order acceptance restrictions in Rule 11.1(a)(1) so that they apply prior to 7:00 a.m. or, if later, prior to the order's designated Start Time. The Exchange is not proposing any change to the categories of orders subject to these restrictions, which will continue to be: orders with a Post Only instruction, ISOs, Market Orders other than those with a TIF instruction of Regular Hours Only or a Stop Price, orders with a Minimum Execution Quantity instruction that also include a TIF instruction of Regular Hours Only, and all orders with a TIF instruction of IOC or FOK. The Exchange is also retaining the existing 7:00 a.m. threshold. Under the proposal, an order in one of these categories designated with a Start Time later than 7:00 a.m. will not be accepted prior to its Start Time. The current restrictions are designed to limit certain order types that are not suitable for queueing to the period in which an order is eligible for execution. Tying the restrictions to an order's designated Start Time applies that same rationale to the more flexible Start Time framework. EDGX similarly ties the same five categories of restrictions to the period before orders become eligible for execution, which on EDGX is the Order Acceptance Queueing Time.
[
19
]
The Exchange is not proposing to change its order entry window, which will continue to begin at 6:00 a.m., or the Time in Force instructions available to Users. Orders entered prior to the Early Trading Session without a Start Time designation will continue to become eligible for execution at the start of the Early Trading Session, Pre-Opening Session, or Regular Trading Hours, depending on the Time in Force selected by the User. Use of the Start Time instruction is optional.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to the Exchange and, in particular, the requirements of Section 6(b) of the Act.
[
20
]
Specifically, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5)
[
21
]
requirements that the rules of an exchange be designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in regulating, clearing, settling, processing information with respect to, and facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system, and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest. Additionally, the Exchange believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the Section 6(b)(5) requirement that the rules of an exchange not be designed to permit unfair discrimination between customers, issuers, brokers, or dealers.
The Exchange believes the proposed Start Time instruction removes impediments to and perfects the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system because it replaces the single fixed point at which orders entered prior to the Early Trading Session become eligible for execution with a flexible and uniform framework. Under that framework, Users may control the time at which their orders become eligible for execution prior to Regular Trading Hours. The Commission approved the same Start Time framework for EDGX, which replaced EDGX's 4:00 a.m. Start and 7:00 a.m. Start construct.
[
22
]
The Start Time instruction provides Members with additional flexibility to manage the timing of their order flow in the period before Regular Trading Hours. This includes aligning order eligibility with anticipated market conditions or with their own trading strategies, without requiring Members to manually enter orders at a particular time.
The Exchange believes the proposed time-sequencing provision promotes just and equitable principles of trade and protects investors because orders that become eligible at the commencement of the Early Trading Session or at a given Start Time will be handled in a transparent and objective manner, in time sequence beginning with the order with the oldest time stamp. This is the same manner in which orders are handled today at the commencement of the Early Trading Session, and it is consistent with the sequencing provision approved for EDGX.
The Exchange believes that tying the existing order acceptance restrictions to the later of 7:00 a.m. or the order's designated Start Time protects investors
(
printed page 69026)
and the public interest. The proposal preserves the existing categories of restricted orders and the existing 7:00 a.m. threshold. It applies those restrictions consistently to orders that will not be eligible for execution until a later Start Time, ensuring that order types that are not suitable for queueing are not accepted before the order may execute. The proposed rule change does not loosen any existing restriction.
The proposed rule change also promotes consistency across the Cboe-affiliated equities exchanges, which reduces complexity for Members that access multiple Cboe-affiliated exchanges and fosters cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities. The proposed rule change does not permit unfair discrimination because the Start Time instruction will be available to all Members on the same terms, and its use is optional.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intramarket competition because the Start Time instruction will be available to all Members on an equal and non-discriminatory basis, and its use is optional. The Exchange does not believe the proposed rule change will impose any burden on intermarket competition because it is based on a rule that the Commission approved for EDGX, and it is designed to provide Members with consistent order handling functionality across the Cboe-affiliated equities exchanges rather than to address any competitive issue. Other exchanges are free to adopt similar functionality.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
The Exchange neither solicited nor received comments on the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
Because the foregoing proposed rule change does not:
A. significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest;
B. impose any significant burden on competition; and
C. become operative for 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, it has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
23
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)
[
24
]
thereunder. At any time within 60 days of the filing of the proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission will institute proceedings to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-CboeEDGA-2026-035  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeEDGA-2026-035. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-CboeEDGA-2026-035 and should be submitted on or before November 23, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
25
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106752; File No. SR-NYSETEX-2026-38]
October 28, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1)
[
1
]
of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
2
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
3
]
notice is hereby given that, on October 15, 2026, the NYSE Texas, Inc. (“NYSE Texas” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend the title, Article II, Sections 1, 2 and 3, Article IV, Section 7, and Article IX, Section 1, of the bylaws of the Exchange to (a) replace the term “Permit Holders” with “Participants,” (b) clarify the definition of “Participant,” (c) remove the requirement that the fair representation director be a Participant, and (d) make a conforming change. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend the title, Article II, Sections 1 (Powers), 2 (General Composition and Term of Office) and 3 (Nomination and Election), Article IV, Section 7 (Nominating Committee), and Article IX, Section 1 (Management of the Corporation), of the bylaws of the Exchange to (a) replace the term “Permit Holders” with “Participants,” (b) clarify the definition of “Participant,” (c) remove the requirement that the fair representation director be a Participant, and (d) make a conforming change.
Replacing Permit Holders With Participants
The Exchange Act requires that every exchange have rules that “assure a fair representation of its members in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs”.
[
4
]
In compliance with this requirement, the Exchange's bylaws set forth the process by which its fair representation directors, the “Non-Affiliated Directors,” are chosen.
Currently, the bylaws provide that Permit Holders nominate the Non-Affiliated Directors, may submit a different candidate, vote on contested nominations for Non-Affiliated Directors, and serve on the Nominating Committee.
[
5
]
“Permit Holders” are defined as “trading permit holders who are permitted to trade on the [Exchange]'s facilities for the trading of equities that are securities as covered by the Exchange Act.”
[
6
]
The Exchange recently made a filing to add a new membership category known as “Limited Underwriting Members.” Limited Underwriting Members are a type of non-trading Exchange membership solely for the limited purpose of acting as a principal underwriter of an underwritten public offering.
[
7
]
As such, they do not have trading permits, and so are not Permit Holders, but are members under the Exchange Act.
[
8
]
Accordingly, to ensure that all “members” (as defined in the Exchange Act) have “fair representation . . . in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs”
[
9
]
the Exchange proposes to amend Article II, Sections 1, 2 and 3, and Article IV, Section 7 of the bylaws of the Exchange in order to replace references to “Permit Holders” with “Participants.”
The proposed changes would make the bylaws consistent with the New York Stock Exchange LLC, an affiliate of the Exchange, which does not require a member be a permit holder in order to participate in the selection of fair representation directors.
[
10
]
Definition of Participant
Currently, “Participant” is defined twice: in Article II, Section 1 as an “individual, corporation, partnership or
(
printed page 69006)
other entity that holds a permit issued by the [Exchange] to trade securities on the market operated by the [Exchange]”; and in Article IX, Section 1, as a “member[ ], as that term is defined in Section 3 of the Exchange Act”.
The Exchange believes that these definitions are consistent, but for the avoidance of doubt and in case they become inconsistent, it proposes to replace the first definition with the second (and remove the definition from Article IX, Section 1). At the same time, it proposes to remove the reference to Section 3 of the Exchange Act and simply provide that “Participant” means “any member as defined in the Exchange Act.”
Nominating Committee
The Exchange proposes to remove the requirement, in the first sentence of Article II, Section 3(b), that the Nominating Committee publish the name of a Participant as its nominee for Non-Affiliated Director. Rather, it would be able to name the individual of its choice as its nominee.
Currently, the Nominating Committee is limited to someone who is currently a Participant. For example, the Nominating Committee cannot name someone who was until recently, but is not at present, a Participant. The proposed change would give the Nominating Committee more options: they still could name a Participant but could name another person as well.
The proposed change would be consistent with the New York Stock Exchange LLC and NYSE American LLC, affiliates of the Exchange, which have no equivalent requirement.
[
11
]
The Exchange notes that the proposed change also would be consistent with the governing documents of other self-regulatory organizations, such as the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC
[
12
]
and CBOE BYX Exchange, Inc.
[
13
]
Non-Substantive Change
The Exchange proposes to make a non-substantive technical and conforming change to the title, to add “First Amended and Restated” to it.
Proposed Changes
The Exchange proposes to make the following changes (proposed additions italicized, proposed deletions in brackets):
Article II, Section 1 would be amended to read as follows:
The business and affairs of the Corporation shall be managed by its Board of Directors. The Board of Directors, acting in accordance with the terms of these bylaws and the rules of the Corporation (“rules”), shall be vested with all powers necessary for the governing of the Corporation as an “exchange” within the meaning of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended (the “Exchange Act”), the regulation of the business conduct of any
member as defined in the Exchange Act
[individual, corporation, partnership or other entity that holds a permit issued by the Corporation to trade securities on the market operated by the Corporation] (each, a “Participant”), and the promotion of the welfare, objects and purposes of the Corporation.
Article II, Section 2(a) would be amended to read as follows:
Subject to Section 2(b), the Board shall consist of a number of directors (“Directors”) as determined from time to time by the stockholders; provided that (1) at least fifty percent (50%) of the directors will be persons from the public and will not be, or be affiliated with, a broker-dealer in securities or employed by, or involved in any material business relationship with, the Corporation or its affiliates (“Public Directors”); and (2) at least twenty percent (20%) of the directors shall consist of individuals nominated by the [trading permit holders who are permitted to trade on the Corporation's facilities for the trading of equities that are securities as covered by the Exchange Act (collectively, such individuals “Permit Holders”)]
Participants
(such directors, “Non-Affiliated Directors”). For purposes of calculation of the minimum number of Non-Affiliated Directors, if 20 percent of the Directors is not a whole number, such number of Directors to be nominated and selected by the [Permit Holders]
Participants
will be rounded up to the next whole number. The term of office of a director shall not be affected by any decrease in the authorized number of directors.
Article II, Section 3(b) and (c) would be amended to read as follows:
(b) The Nominating Committee shall publish the name(s) of one or more [Participants]
individuals
as its nominee(s) for Non-Affiliated Directors of the Board of Directors of the Corporation. A director shall qualify as a Public Director or Non-Affiliated Director only so long as such director meets the requirements for that position. The Nominating Committee shall name sufficient nominees so that at least twenty percent (20%) of the Directors consist of Non-Affiliated Directors. The names of the nominees shall be published on a date in each year (the “Announcement Date”) sufficient to accommodate the process described in this Section 3(b). After the name of proposed nominee(s) is published, [Permit Holders]
Participants
in good standing may submit a petition to the Corporation in writing to nominate additional eligible candidate(s) to fill Non-Affiliated Director position(s) during the next term. If a written petition of at least 10 percent of [Permit Holders]
Participants
in good standing is submitted to the Nominating Committee within two weeks after the Announcement Date, such person(s) shall also be nominated by the Nominating Committee; provided, however, that no [Permit Holders]
Participants,
either alone or together with other [Permit Holders]
Participants
that are deemed its affiliates, may account for more than 50% of the signatories to the petition endorsing a particular petition nominee for the Non-Affiliated Director position(s) on the Board of Directors of the Corporation. Each petition for a petition candidate must include a completed questionnaire used to gather information concerning director candidates (the Corporation shall provide the form of questionnaire upon the request of any [Permit Holder]
Participant
). Notwithstanding anything to the contrary, the Nominating Committee shall determine whether any petition candidate is eligible to serve on the Board of Directors (including whether such person is free of any statutory disqualification (as defined in section 3(a)(39) of the Exchange Act)), and such determination shall be final and conclusive.
(c) In the event that the number of nominees exceeds the number of available seats, the Nominating Committee shall submit the contested nomination to the [Permit Holders]
Participants
for selection. [Permit Holders]
Participants
shall be afforded a confidential voting procedure and shall be given no less than 20 calendar days to submit their votes. Each [Permit Holder]
Participant
in good standing may select one nominee for the
(
printed page 69007)
contested seat on the Board of Directors; provided, however that no [Permit Holder]
Participant,
either alone or together with other [Permit Holders]
Participants
who are deemed its affiliates, may account for more than 20% of the votes cast for a particular nominee for the Non-Affiliated Director position(s) on the Board of Directors of the Corporation. With respect to the contested position, the nominee for the Board of Directors receiving the most votes of [Permit Holders]
Participants
shall be submitted by the Nominating Committee to the Board of Directors of the Corporation. Similarly, the Nominating Committee shall submit uncontested nominees to the Board of Directors. Tie votes shall be decided by the Board of Directors at its first meeting following the election.
Article IV, Section 7 would be amended to read as follows:
The Nominating Committee shall consist solely of Non-Affiliated Directors, as defined above, and/or [Permit Holder]
Participant
representatives, and shall be responsible for approving and submitting names of candidates for election to the position of Non-Affiliated Director pursuant to, and in accordance with, Article II, Section 3. “[Permit Holder]
Participant
representative” shall mean an officer, director, employee or agent of a [Permit Holder]
Participant.
Article IX, Section 1 would be amended to read as follows:
In connection with managing the business and affairs of the Corporation, the Board of Directors shall consider applicable requirements for registration as a national securities exchange under Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act, including, without limitation, the requirements that (a) the rules of the Corporation shall be designed to protect investors and the public interest and (b) the Corporation shall be so organized and have the capacity to carry out the purposes of the Exchange Act and to enforce compliance by its [members, as that term is defined in Section 3 of the Exchange Act (such statutory members being referred to in the Corporation's bylaws and rules as “]Participants[”)] and persons associated with Participants, with the provisions of the Exchange Act, the rules and regulations under the Act and the rules of the Corporation.
The title would be amended by adding “First Amended and Restated” to it.
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act,
[
14
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(1)
[
15
]
in particular, in that it enables the Exchange to be so organized as to have the capacity to be able to carry out the purposes of the Exchange Act and to comply, and to enforce compliance by its exchange members and persons associated with its exchange members, with the provisions of the Exchange Act, the rules and regulations thereunder, and the rules of the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(3) of the Exchange Act,
[
16
]
in that it would ensure a fair representation of its members in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs. The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act,
[
17
]
in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
The proposed rule changes replacing “Permit Holders” with “Participants,” conforming the definition of “Participants,” and removing limitations on who can be named by the Nominating Committee (collectively, the “Proposed Changes”) would enable the Exchange to be so organized as to have the capacity to be able to carry out the purposes of the Exchange Act and ensure a fair representation of its members in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs because they would ensure that all members are equal in selecting its Non-Affiliated Directors, whether or not they have a trading permit. The Proposed Changes would allow the Nominating Committee to name the individuals of its choice as its nominees and not be limited to individuals that are currently Participants.
The Proposed Changes would allow the Exchange to ensure that all “members” (as defined in the Exchange Act) have “fair representation . . . in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs”
[
18
]
by including member organizations that do not have trading permits. The Proposed Changes would allow the Exchange to ensure that it remains in compliance with the cited Exchange Act requirement and make the bylaws consistent with the rules of the Exchange.
The Proposed Changes would make the bylaws consistent with the New York Stock Exchange LLC, an affiliate of the Exchange, as it does not require a member be a permit holder in order to participate in the selection of fair representation directors
[
19
]
and neither the New York Stock Exchange LLC nor NYSE American LLC require their nominating committees to limit their nominees.
[
20
]
The proposed rule change to the title and moving up the definition of “Participants” (the “Non-Substantive Changes”) are non-substantive changes that do not impact the governance or ownership of the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed Non-Substantive Changes would enable the Exchange to continue to be so organized as to have the capacity to carry out the purposes of the Exchange Act and comply and enforce compliance with the provisions of the Exchange Act by its members and persons associated with its members, because making the Non-Substantive Changes would contribute to the orderly operation of the Exchange by adding clarity and transparency to its rules.
Further, the Exchange believes that the proposed rule change would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protect investors and the public interest. The Proposed Changes would make the bylaws consistent with the rules of the Exchange and therefore would ensure that market participants can more easily navigate, understand and comply with the governing documents of the Exchange. he proposed Non-Substantive Changes would ensure that market participants can more easily navigate, understand and comply with the governing documents of the Exchange. The proposed rule changes would therefore reduce potential investor or market participant confusion.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Exchange Act. The proposed rule change is not
(
printed page 69008)
intended to address competitive issues but rather is concerned solely with making the bylaws consistent with the rules of the Exchange and making non-substantive changes to the bylaws.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
21
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
22
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder.
[
23
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
24
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSETEX-2026-38  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSETEX-2026-38. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSETEX-2026-38 and should be submitted on or before November 23, 2026.
For the Commission, by the Division of Trading and Markets, pursuant to delegated authority.
[
25
]
Sherry R. Haywood,
Assistant Secretary.

title: Self-Regulatory Organizations; National Securities Clearing Corporation; Notice of Filing and Immediate Effectiveness of a Proposed Rule Change Concerning the Automated Customer Account Transfer Service Account Transfer Process for Insurance and Retirement Products
full_text:

Securities and Exchange Commission
[Release No. 34-106751; File No. SR-NSCC-2026-011]
October 28, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
1
]
and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
2
]
notice is hereby given that on October 16, 2026, National Securities Clearing Corporation (“NSCC”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (“Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I, II and III below, which Items have been prepared by the clearing agency. NSCC filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act
[
3
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(4) thereunder.
[
4
]
The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The proposed rule change amends the NSCC Rules & Procedures (“NSCC Rules”) concerning the Automated Customer Account Transfer Service (“ACATS”) account transfer process for insurance and retirement products.
[
5
]
II. Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the clearing agency included statements concerning the purpose of and basis for the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of these statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The clearing agency has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant aspects of such statements.
(
printed page 68999)
(A) Clearing Agency's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The purpose of this proposed rule change is to amend the NSCC Rules to discontinue certain ACATS functionality for transmitting information necessary to re-register insurance products (
e.g.,
annuities) through NSCC's Insurance & Retirement Solutions (“I&RS”) service and transfer responsibility for insurance product registration and confirmation to NSCC's I&RS services system.
The proposed rule change is discussed in detail below.
Background
ACATS Overview
ACATS is a non-guaranteed service provided by NSCC that enables Members to effect transfers of customer accounts among themselves. ACATS complements Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (“FINRA”) Rule 11870 regarding customer account transfers, which requires FINRA members to use automated clearing agency customer account transfer services and to effect customer account transfers within specified time frames.
[
6
]
ACATS automates and standardizes procedures for the transfer of assets in a customer account, allowing Members to efficiently and automatically enter, review, and generate instructions to settle customer account transfers. The timing and procedures with respect to ACATS customer account transfers are intended to be consistent with the timing and processes set forth in FINRA Rule 11870.
ACATS provides functionality for account transfers that include I&RS Products such as annuities (referred to as the “ACATS/Insurance Processing Service” or “ACATS/IPS”).
[
7
]
ACATS/IPS automates the changes in distributors of record for an annuity when clients transfer their accounts from one brokerage firm to another. ACATS/IPS enables distributors to include annuity assets, along with other securities, when transferring accounts and gives them automated, timely access to important information about their customers' portfolios. The service also facilitates representative of record and broker-identification number changes within a contract.
ACATS is primarily described in NSCC Rule 50 and Procedure XVIII of the NSCC Rules.
[
8
]
Pursuant to NSCC Rule 50, an NSCC Member to whom a customer's account will be transferred (the “Receiving Member”) initiates the transfer by submitting a transfer initiation request to NSCC, which contains the customer detail information that the NSCC Member who currently has the account (the “Delivering Member”) requires to transfer the account.
[
9
]
The Delivering Member must either reject the customer account transfer request or submit detailed customer account asset data to NSCC.
[
10
]
NSCC then provides a report detailing the customer account asset data to the Receiving Member,
[
11
]
who has one business day after receipt of the report to review the account and: (i) accept all assets; (ii) reject one or more assets, to the extent such a rejection is permitted by the Receiving Member's Designated Examining Authority (
i.e.,
FINRA), and allow the transfer of the remaining assets; (iii) request the Delivering Member to make adjustments to the customer account asset list; or (iv) reject the account, to extent such a rejection is permitted by NSCC or FINRA.
[
12
]
Once a customer account has been accepted by the Receiving Member, ACATS facilitates the settlements associated with the account transfer at the appropriate asset settling location (
e.g.,
through NSCC's Continuous Net Settlement system (“CNS”) for CNS-eligible securities, DTC for securities otherwise eligible for DTC settlement services, Fund/SERV for eligible mutual fund products, or I&RS for annuities).
Currently, Members utilize ACATS to both identify insurance products (primarily annuities) to be included in an account transfer and to manage the registration changes for those assets with broker-dealers and insurance carriers. Pursuant to Section 8 of NSCC Rule 50, if I&RS Eligible Products (or “I&RS Products”) are to be transferred the Receiving Member shall, within one (1) Business Day after receipt from NSCC of the report detailing the I&RS Products data or simultaneous with the submission of an acceleration instruction, submit to NSCC detailed transfer instructions, which are processed through I&RS in accordance with Section 6 of NSCC Rule 57.
[
13
]
Each day NSCC also produces a report to the Receiving and Delivering Member, indicating the I&RS Eligible Products transfers which have been confirmed or rejected by the Insurance Carrier/Retirement Services Member in accordance with Section 6 of NSCC Rule 57, or which have been deleted.
[
14
]
NSCC is proposing changes to Section 8 of NSCC Rule 50 in connection with the proposed enhancements discussed herein.
Proposed Changes
NSCC proposes to modify the NSCC Rules to enhance the account transfer process for I&RS Products. As discussed above, ACATS is currently responsible for both identifying insurance products to be included in an account transfer and managing registration changes with broker-dealers and insurance carriers. NSCC proposes to enhance this process by transferring responsibility for insurance product re-registration and confirmation to NSCC's I&RS services system. ACATS would continue to allow firms to initiate and submit insurance assets for transfers but would pass those assets on to the I&RS system to complete the transfer process. The proposed change would streamline and simplify operational processes for Members by aligning the ACATS process for account transfers to the standard operational process used for insurance product re-registrations in the I&RS service.
Under the proposal, Members would continue to use ACATS to initiate a transfer, Delivering Members would continue to use ACATS to add insurance assets to a transfer, and ACATS would validate that the CUSIP and Receiving Member are ACATS/IPS eligible. However, the remaining processing of the re-registration and transfer of such assets would be completed through NSCC's I&RS service. Under the proposed enhancements, Receiving Members would receive a notification from I&RS that a broker-dealer of record change is required in connection with an account transfer, the Receiving Member would
(
printed page 69000)
send the broker-dealer of record change directly to the I&RS system, I&RS would send data to Insurance Carrier and the Carrier would confirm back to I&RS, and I&RS would send a confirmation to the Receiving Member.
In connection with the proposed enhancements, NSCC would decommission a number of ACATS instructions, files and records, which would no longer be needed when these processes move to the I&RS system. This includes, for example, the decommissioning of (i) the Insurance Registration (IR) Record, which facilitates the re-registration of annuity assets; (ii) the insurance statistics file to confirm accepted and rejected transactions by the insurance carrier; and (iii) Receiver and Deliver (R&D) Insurance Instructions for IR records that were either rejected by the insurance carrier or not completed within twenty business days. Eligible assets would continue to be assigned to the I&RS services system when both the CUSIP and receiving broker qualify for I&RS processing.
In connection with the proposed changes, NSCC would remove references to I&RS Products and certain associated instructions and reports concerning I&RS Product transfers from Section 8 of NSCC Rule 50. Specifically, NSCC would modify Section 8 of NSCC Rule 50 to remove references to I&RS Products as products for which a Receiving Member must provide detailed transfer instructions through ACATS. Under the proposed enhancements, these instructions would be processed through the I&RS service and would no longer be processed through the ACATS system. NSCC would also modify Section 8 of Rule 50 to delete rule text describing the daily issuance of reports by NSCC to the Receiving and Delivering Member indicating the I&RS Eligible Products transfers which have been confirmed or rejected by the Insurance Carrier/Retirement Services Member in accordance with Section 6 of NSCC Rule 57, or which have been deleted. These reports would no longer be applicable under the enhanced I&RS Product transfer process.
NSCC notes that the ACATS/IPS service has seen only modest adoption and usage since its introduction in 2005. Fewer than ten Members currently use the ACATS/IPS service to process transfers of insurance products (particularly annuities) through the I&RS services system. These Members are also current users of the I&RS service. As NSCC continues to modernize its systems, NSCC believes that there is a substantial opportunity to improve and refine existing ACATS processes and potentially expand the volume of I&RS Products transferred via the ACATS platform. As noted above, the proposed change would streamline and simplify operational processes for Members by aligning the ACATS process for account transfers to the standard operational process used for annuity re-registrations in the I&RS service. This in turn may reduce the burden of maintaining separate processes for ACATS and non-ACATS re-registrations and encourage further use of the ACATS platform for account transfers. NSCC has performed outreach to Members currently using the ACATS/IPS service to inform them of the changes and assist in their transition to the new process for transferring I&RS Products.
[
15
]
Implementation Timeframe
NSCC would implement the proposed rule change on November 20, 2026.
2. Statutory Basis
NSCC believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of the Act and the rules and regulations thereunder applicable to a registered clearing agency. Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act
[
16
]
requires that the rules of a clearing agency be designed to, among other things, promote the prompt and accurate clearance and settlement of securities transactions. NSCC believes the proposed rule change is consistent with the requirements of Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act for the reasons stated below.
As described above, NSCC is working with the industry to enhance the account transfer process for I&RS Products by transferring responsibility for insurance product registration and confirmation from ACATS to NSCC's I&RS services system. Members would continue to have the ability to initiate account transfers for I&RS Products within ACATS, but ACATS would then pass those assets on to the I&RS system to complete the transfer process. The proposed change would streamline and simplify the operational processes for Members by aligning the ACATS process for account transfers to the standard operational process used for insurance product re-registrations in the I&RS service. This in turn may reduce the burden of maintaining separate processes for ACATS and non-ACATS re-registration and encourage further use of the ACATS platform for account transfers. As a result, NSCC believes the proposed rule change would promote the prompt and accurate settlement of account transfers involving insurance products, consistent with the requirements of Section 17A(b)(3)(F) of the Act.
[
17
]
(B) Clearing Agency's Statement on Burden on Competition
Section 17A(b)(3)(I) of the Act
[
18
]
requires that the rules of the clearing agency do not impose any burden on competition not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the Act. The proposed rule change is designed to streamline and simplify operational processes for Members by aligning the ACATS process for account transfers to the standard operational process used for insurance product re-registrations in the I&RS service. While the proposed rule change would decommission certain ACATS functionality used by Members to transfer I&RS Products, those Members would continue to have the ability to initiate account transfers for accounts containing I&RS Products within ACATS and to complete the processing of such transfers using NSCC's I&RS service. This simplified process may in turn reduce the burden of maintaining separate processes for ACATS and non-ACATS re-registrations and encourage further use of the ACATS platform for account transfers. NSCC therefore believes the proposed rule change would not impose any burden on competition.
(C) Clearing Agency's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
NSCC has not received or solicited any written comments relating to this proposal. If any written comments are received, they will be publicly filed as an Exhibit 2 to this filing, as required by Form 19b-4 and the General Instructions thereto.
Persons submitting comments are cautioned that, according to Section IV (Solicitation of Comments) of the Exhibit 1A in the General Instructions to Form 19b-4, the Commission does not edit personal identifying information from comment submissions. Commenters should submit only information that they wish to make available publicly, including their name, email address, and any other identifying information.
(
printed page 69001)
All prospective commenters should follow the Commission's instructions on how to submit comments,
available at
www.sec.gov/​rules-regulations/​how-submit-comment
.
General questions regarding the rule filing process or logistical questions regarding this filing should be directed to the Main Office of the Commission's Division of Trading and Markets at

[Release No. 34-106750; File No. SR-NYSEARCA-2026-105]
October 28, 2026.
Pursuant to Section 19(b)(1)
[
1

of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934 (“Act”)
[
2

and Rule 19b-4 thereunder,
[
3
]
notice is hereby given that on October 15, 2026, NYSE Arca, Inc. (“NYSE Arca” or the “Exchange”) filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission (the “Commission”) the proposed rule change as described in Items I and II below, which Items have been prepared by the self-regulatory organization. The Commission is publishing this notice to solicit comments on the proposed rule change from interested persons.
I. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Terms of Substance of the Proposed Rule Change
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 3.2(b)(3)(C)(ii) so that the nominating committee may name any individuals as its nominees for the board of directors of the Exchange. The proposed rule change is available on the Exchange's website at
www.nyse.com
and at the principal office of the Exchange.
II. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
In its filing with the Commission, the self-regulatory organization included statements concerning the purpose of, and basis for, the proposed rule change and discussed any comments it received on the proposed rule change. The text of those statements may be examined at the places specified in Item IV below. The Exchange has prepared summaries, set forth in sections A, B, and C below, of the most significant parts of such statements.
A. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement of the Purpose of, and the Statutory Basis for, the Proposed Rule Change
1. Purpose
The Exchange proposes to amend Rule 3.2(b)(3)(C)(ii) (Exchange Committees) so that the nominating committee may name any individuals as its nominees for the board of directors (“Board”) of the Exchange.
Currently, the first sentence of Rule 3.2(b)(3)(C)(ii) provides that the Nominating Committee
[
4
]
shall “publish the name of one (1) or more OTP Holders or Associated Persons of an OTP Firm or ETP Holder or Associated Persons of an ETP Holder as its nominee(s)”
[
5
]
for non-affiliated directors of the Board of the Excahange.
This limits the Nominating Committee in naming the individuals of its choice: it can only name someone who is
currently
an OTP Holder or Associated Person of an OTP Firm or ETP Holder or Associated Person of an ETP Holder. For example, if someone was until recently, but is not at present, an Associated Person of an OTP Firm or Associated Person of an ETP Holder, the Nominating Committee cannot name them as a candidate.
The Exchange proposes to amend the first sentence of Rule 3.2(b)(3)(C)(ii) so that the Nominating Committee may name individuals of its choice as nominees. More specifically, the Exchange proposes to make the following change (proposed deletion bracketed, proposed addition underlined):
The Nominating Committee shall publish the name of one (1) or more [OTP Holders or Associated Persons of an OTP Firm or ETP Holder or Associated Persons of an ETP Holder]
individuals
as its nominee(s) for Non-Affiliated Directors of the Board of Directors of the NYSE Arca, Inc.
The proposed change would be consistent with the New York Stock
(
printed page 69004)
Exchange LLC and NYSE American LLC, affiliates of the Exchange, which have no equivalent requirement.
[
6
]
The Exchange notes that the proposed changes also would be consistent with the governing documents of other self-regulatory organizations, such as the Nasdaq Stock Market LLC
[
7
]
and CBOE BYX Exchange, Inc.
[
8
]
2. Statutory Basis
The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b) of the Exchange Act,
[
9
]
in general, and furthers the objectives of Section 6(b)(1)
[
10
]
in particular, in that it enables the Exchange to be so organized as to have the capacity to be able to carry out the purposes of the Exchange Act and to comply, and to enforce compliance by its exchange members and persons associated with its exchange members, with the provisions of the Exchange Act, the rules and regulations thereunder, and the rules of the Exchange. The Exchange believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(3) of the Exchange Act,
[
11
]
in that it would ensure a fair representation of its members in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs. The Exchange also believes that the proposed rule change is consistent with Section 6(b)(5) of the Exchange Act,
[
12
]
in that it is designed to prevent fraudulent and manipulative acts and practices, to promote just and equitable principles of trade, to foster cooperation and coordination with persons engaged in facilitating transactions in securities, to remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, to protect investors and the public interest.
The Exchange believes that the change would enable it to be so organized as to have the capacity to be able to carry out the purposes of the Exchange Act and would ensure a fair representation of its members in the selection of its directors and administration of its affairs because it would allow the Nominating Committee to name the individuals of its choice as its nominees, and not be limited to individuals that are currently OTP Holders or Associated Persons of an OTP Firm or ETP Holder or Associated Persons of an ETP Holder. The proposed changes would allow the Exchange to ensure that it remains in compliance with the cited Exchange Act requirement.
[
13
]
The Exchange believes that for the same reason the rule change would remove impediments to and perfect the mechanism of a free and open market and a national market system and, in general, protect investors and the public interest, as it would remove the limitation, and therefore give the Nominating Committee more options.
The Exchange believes these changes are non-controversial and raise no novel regulatory, governance, or competitive issues. The proposed rule change would be consistent with the New York Stock Exchange LLC and NYSE American LLC, affiliates of the Exchange, neither of which require their nominating committees to limit their nominees.
[
14
]
The proposed change is intended solely to harmonize the Exchange's rules with an existing governance framework that has already been established and subject to regulatory review.
B. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Burden on Competition
The Exchange does not believe that the proposed rule change will impose any burden on competition that is not necessary or appropriate in furtherance of the purposes of the Exchange Act. The proposed rule change is not intended to address competitive issues but rather is concerned solely with ensuring that the Nominating Committee has more options in naming its nominees.
C. Self-Regulatory Organization's Statement on Comments on the Proposed Rule Change Received From Members, Participants, or Others
No written comments were solicited or received with respect to the proposed rule change.
III. Date of Effectiveness of the Proposed Rule Change and Timing for Commission Action
The Exchange has filed the proposed rule change pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A)(iii) of the Act
[
15
]
and Rule 19b-4(f)(6) thereunder.
[
16
]
Because the proposed rule change does not: (i) significantly affect the protection of investors or the public interest; (ii) impose any significant burden on competition; and (iii) become operative prior to 30 days from the date on which it was filed, or such shorter time as the Commission may designate, if consistent with the protection of investors and the public interest, the proposed rule change has become effective pursuant to Section 19(b)(3)(A) of the Act and Rule 19b-4(f)(6)(iii) thereunder.
[
17
]
At any time within 60 days of the filing of such proposed rule change, the Commission summarily may temporarily suspend such rule change if it appears to the Commission that such action is necessary or appropriate in the public interest, for the protection of investors, or otherwise in furtherance of the purposes of the Act. If the Commission takes such action, the Commission shall institute proceedings under Section 19(b)(2)(B)
[
18
]
of the Act to determine whether the proposed rule change should be approved or disapproved.
IV. Solicitation of Comments
Interested persons are invited to submit written data, views and arguments concerning the foregoing, including whether the proposed rule change is consistent with the Act. Comments may be submitted by any of the following methods:
Electronic Comments
Use the Commission's internet comment form (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
); or
Send an email to
rule-comments@sec.gov
.
Please include file number SR-NYSEARCA-2026-105  on the subject line.
Paper Comments
Send paper comments in triplicate to Secretary, Securities and Exchange
(
printed page 69005)
Commission, 100 F Street NE, Washington, DC 20549-1090.
All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEARCA-2026-105. This file number should be included on the subject line if email is used. To help the Commission process and review your comments more efficiently, please use only one method. The Commission will post all comments on the Commission's internet website (
https://www.sec.gov/​rules/​sro.shtml
). Copies of the filing will be available for inspection and copying at the principal office of the Exchange. Do not include personal identifiable information in submissions; you should submit only information that you wish to make available publicly. We may redact in part or withhold entirely from publication submitted material that is obscene or subject to copyright protection. All submissions should refer to file number SR-NYSEARCA-2026-105 and should be submitted on or before November 23, 2026.

]
